port.name: Aider
port.description: Living Code for Aider: native YAML colors for user and assistant messages, warnings, errors and completion-menu states.

guide.installation:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/living-code-theme/aider.git
cd aider
```

Try one flavor from this clone:

```sh
aider --config "$PWD/themes/living-code-night.yml"
```

For everyday use, merge the nine color settings from the selected file into your existing `~/.aider.conf.yml` or project `.aider.conf.yml`. Keep model, credentials and editing settings unchanged.
guide.configuration: The files map exactly Aider’s nine documented `*-color` options. Do not combine them with `--dark-mode` or `--light-mode`, which replace these colors with Aider presets. This port intentionally leaves `code-theme` alone so it does not replace your syntax theme with an unrelated preset. Completion foreground/background and the selected entry are explicitly paired.
guide.compatibility: For Aider versions exposing the nine color flags listed in `test/fixtures/upstream.json`. This is a UI-color port, not a custom Pygments style. Aider’s rendered code blocks continue to use your configured `code-theme`; the terminal owns the full-screen background. Use a matching Living Code terminal theme for the rest of the palette. Tests parse native YAML and verify accepted flag names and semantic colors.
